title: Builder Bricktopher Brings Star Wars to Life in Microscale
summary: Fan builder Bricktopher has created a series of microscale Star Wars scenes, from Naboo's Theed to the Battle of Hoth, showcasing clever part use and scale.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
A builder known as Bricktopher has shared a set of microscale Star Wars creations, as featured by The Brothers Brick. The scenes include Theed on Naboo (complete with tiny N1 Starfighters built from Technic bushes, a T-bar and a minifig hand), the Death Star trench run, a Star Destroyer looming over Jedha, a Battle of Hoth vignette with Snowspeeders and AT-AT segments, and the destruction of Tipoca City on Kamino.

Each build leans into clever part usage — from hidden studs for a clean 'model kit' look to hairpieces standing in for laser fire — to capture iconic moments from the films in a compact scale.

## Why it matters
Microscale building is a great way to showcase big cinematic moments without needing huge amounts of space or parts, and this collection is a good example of creative part reuse and scene composition for anyone interested in display builds, custom models or Star Wars-themed brick projects.

## What to watch next
Fans of these builds may want to keep an eye on Bricktopher's future work or similar microscale Star Wars creations shared across the brick-building community.

title: Fan-built LEGO Meduseld brings Rohan's Golden Hall to life
summary: Builder monsieur.kek has created a striking MOC of Meduseld, the Golden Hall of Rohan from Lord of the Rings, filling a gap left since the 2012 Helm's Deep sets.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
Fan builder monsieur.kek has unveiled a large-scale custom LEGO model (MOC) of Meduseld, the Golden Hall of King Théoden from The Lord of the Rings. According to The Brothers Brick, the build uses SNOT (studs not on top) techniques to create wood-effect pillars and walls, stacked cheese slopes for texture beneath the golden arches, and a tan tiled roof echoing the style seen on the official LEGO Rivendell set.

The model includes custom minifigures of King Théoden - using the hair piece from the new Unicorn Elf collectible minifigure - and Éowyn, a character rarely seen in minifig form. The whole build sits on an elevated stone platform designed for minifig display.

This is a fan creation, not an official LEGO Group set.

## Why it matters
The official LEGO Lord of the Rings range has recently expanded with Minas Tirith, but Rohirrim-themed sets have been thin on the ground since 2012's Helm's Deep and Uruk-Hai Army. This MOC shows how the fan community is filling that gap with impressive scale and detail, and offers inspiration for anyone wanting to build their own Middle-earth display pieces.

## What to watch next
No word yet on official LEGO plans for more Rohan-themed sets, but fan interest in this era of Middle-earth could be a hint at demand LEGO might eventually respond to.

title: BrickLink Designer Program to change again for 2028 submissions
summary: BrickLink has confirmed fresh changes to its Designer Program, with the first round of 2028 submissions opening this autumn.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
BrickLink has officially confirmed that its BrickLink Designer Program (BDP) is changing again, with the new format kicking off when the first 2028 submission window opens this Fall.

The BDP has a history of evolving. It grew out of an earlier AFOL Designer Program from 2018, before BrickLink (working with LEGO Group as its parent company) launched the BDP proper in 2021. That first version ran as three rounds of crowd-funded competitions between LEGO Ideas sets that narrowly missed out on the official 10k club threshold.

The program was then relaunched in early 2024 with a different structure: multiple curated submission rounds each year from fan designers, working within a limited part and colour palette and strict submission rules.

Brickset notes that change has been a constant theme of the program so far, and this latest update continues that pattern ahead of 2028. The full details of what's changing weren't fully outlined in the available source material, so exact rule changes should be checked directly with BrickLink before being reported as confirmed specifics.

## Why it matters
The BDP is one of the main routes for fan designers to get original creations turned into official, buildable sets through BrickLink. Any changes to submission rules, timing or format directly affect AFOL creators, Ideas fans and collectors who follow the program's output each year.

## What to watch next
Brick fans should keep an eye on BrickLink's own channels for the full breakdown of the new 2028 rules, including submission windows, part palettes and eligibility criteria, once they're published in full.

title: LEGO Insiders Days promotions now live, including free Sea Serpent set
summary: LEGO's annual Insiders Days event has kicked off on LEGO.com, bringing gifts-with-purchase, double points on selected themes and regional discounts.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
LEGO's yearly Insiders Days promotions are now running on LEGO.com. UK shoppers spending over £160 can add 40912 Sea Serpent to their basket as a free gift, while a £90 spend on Creator, City or Friends sets unlocks the 5010033 Airplane – Special Edition as a bonus build.

On top of the gifts-with-purchase, several themes are earning double Insiders points for the duration of the promotion, including Sonic the Hedgehog, Jurassic World, Speed Champions, Harry Potter, Marvel, Disney, Wicked and Education sets.

Discounts are also part of the event, though these vary by region. European examples flagged so far include 20% off 10323 PAC-MAN Arcade and a discount on 10337 Lamborghini, with more reductions likely to appear as the promotion continues.

## Why it matters
Insiders Days is one of the bigger recurring promotional windows on LEGO.com, and free GWP sets like the Sea Serpent tend to be popular with collectors who like completing themed extras. Double points events are also a handy way to boost your Insiders rewards balance ahead of future redemptions.

## What to watch next
Exact discount lists and thresholds can differ between the UK, US and EU stores, so it's worth checking LEGO.com directly for your region's current offers, and keeping an eye out for further set-specific discounts as the promotion rolls on.

title: LEGO Pokémon range grows with first-ever minifigures
summary: The LEGO Group and The Pokémon Company International have officially confirmed five new LEGO Pokémon sets, including a Poké Ball set that introduces the first LEGO Pokémon minifigures.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
The LEGO Group and The Pokémon Company International have officially announced five new additions to the LEGO Pokémon range, which launched in March with a series of large-scale buildable creatures. According to the confirmed press release, the new wave includes further creature-style builds alongside a Poké Ball set that, for the first time, features LEGO Pokémon minifigures and Pokémon figures.

Exact set numbers, pricing and full contents haven't been detailed in the excerpt available, but the announcement confirms this is an expansion of the existing LEGO Pokémon build-and-display line rather than a rumoured concept.

## Why it matters
Minifigures are a huge part of what makes LEGO collectable and displayable, so their arrival in the Pokémon range is a significant step for the theme. It signals LEGO and The Pokémon Company International see long-term potential here, likely opening the door to more sets, characters and trainer-style builds down the line — good news for collectors and display builders alike.

## What to watch next
Keep an eye out for official set numbers, images and pricing as LEGO typically follows these press announcements with retailer listings. It's also worth watching whether more minifigures or trainer characters get added to future waves.
